summary: Baladora Indrajothi works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA, MPhil, and Hindi diploma from the University of Kelaniya, where he was a Junior Fellow (2016–2019), and later lectured at Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka (2019–2021).

Balaganapathi Devarakonda is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Delhi (MA 1993–1995) and the University of Hyderabad (PhD 1997–2004), and served as a professor at the University of Delhi in 2015.

Baliram Shukla works in the fields of philosophy and Indology. He has held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, serving as Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and as professor (attested 2026).
Balram Shukla is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Delhi and held an appointment there as professor in 2004.

Balthasar Bickel specializes in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Zurich (~1985–1997), taught at the University of Leipzig (~2002–2011), and served on an editorial board at the University of Zurich around 2011.

Bangwei Wang is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. He earned his doctorate at Peking University in 1987, where he served as Professor (attested 2000–2007), Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies (attested 2017), and Boya Retired Professor (attested 2026).

Banikanta Kakati was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, then served as professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and department head and dean at Gauhati University in 1948.

Bapu Deva Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundiraja Misra, and Sevarama. He served as a teacher at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara A. Holdrege is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, including Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and Professor (attested 2026).

Barbara Ambros specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning degrees from Columbia and Harvard, she taught at institutions including International Christian University and Columbia, becoming a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2015.

Barbara Catharina Jacoba Timmer was an Indologist and philosopher. She studied at Leiden University and completed her PhD at the University of Amsterdam (~1922–1930), where she studied under Barend Faddegon, Jean Philippe Vogel, and Marcel Cohen.

Barbara Diane Miller worked in Tibetology and other fields. She completed a BA at the University of Michigan and a PhD at the University of Washington, later teaching at Beloit College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1989).

Barbara E. Ward was a sinologist who studied at Cambridge, the University of London, and the London School of Economics. She taught at the University of London, Cambridge, Cornell, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her DPhil from the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel, later working at Humboldt University of Berlin, Oxford, and the University of Vienna.

Barbara Harriss-White is a scholar of Indology and development studies who attended Newstead Wood School. She held posts at the University of East Anglia (~1979–1989), Queen Elizabeth House (~1990–2011), and the University of Oxford and Wolfson College (~1990).

Barbara Mittler is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Pearson College London, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University, joining Heidelberg University in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a BA from Queen's University at Kingston and a PhD in social anthropology at SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran.

Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist who studied at Barnard, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch. She served as professor at Columbia and Barnard College, and as president of the Association for Asian Studies.

Barbora Sojková specializes in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. She studied at Charles University, UCL, and the University of Oxford, holding postdoctoral researcher posts at the University of Oxford and the University of Zurich in 2025.

Barbra R. Clayton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and also studied under G. Raj. She was affiliated with Mount Allison University in 2013.
